items.title: AI memory with biological decay (52% recall)
items.raw_excerpt: Most RAG setups fail because they treat memory like a static filing cabinet. When every transient bug fix or abandoned rule is stored forever, the context window eventually chokes on noise, spiking token costs and degrading the agent's reasoning. This implementation experiments with a biological approach by using the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve to manage context as a living substrate. Memories are assigned a "strength" score where each recall reinforces the data and flattens its decay curve (spaced repetition), while unused data eventually hits a threshold and is pruned. To solve the "logical neighbor" problem where semantic search misses relevant but non-similar nodes, a graph layer is layered over the vector store. excerpt_i18n.en: The underlying logic of AI development is shifting this year. The momentum has not waned but is accelerating. More importantly, AI is transitioning from a "capability competition" to "system deployment"—how to operate stably, evolve continuously, and truly embed into human society and industrial systems in the real world. A new generation of system paradigms, represented by agents, is emerging. AI is no longer just a tool for generating content but is gradually integrating into workflows, with capabilities for continuous perception, decision-making, and execution. From "answering questions" to "completing tasks," from single-turn interactions to long-sequence closed loops, AI is evolving into a system form that participates in actions and decisions. Meanwhile, world models oriented toward the physical world are accelerating development. From multimodal understanding to spatial and dynamic modeling, AI is beginning to depict the evolution laws and causal mechanisms of the real world with "states" as the core, moving from "generating symbols" to "interacting with the physical world." Agents require stronger world modeling capabilities to execute stably in complex environments, while world models need actions and feedback to form closed-loop learning and continuous optimization. Thus, AI development enters a new phase—"intelligent systems" capable of operating in the real world. However, alongside capability leaps, a series of critical issues are becoming increasingly prominent, including how to construct next-generation AI technology pathways and future system forms, how to embed alignment and governance upfront rather than as post-hoc fixes, and how to achieve intelligent business closed loops. The 8th Beijing Zhiyuan Conference will address these topics.

Un cambio más importante es que la IA está pasando de una "competencia de capacidades" a una "implementación sistémica": cómo operar de manera estable en el mundo real, evolucionar continuamente e integrarse realmente en la sociedad humana y los sistemas industriales. Está surgiendo un nuevo paradigma sistémico representado por los agentes inteligentes. La IA ya no es solo una herramienta para generar contenido, sino que se integra gradualmente en los flujos de trabajo, con capacidades de percepción continua, toma de decisiones y ejecución. Desde "responder preguntas" hasta "completar tareas", desde interacciones únicas hasta bucles cerrados de larga duración, la inteligencia artificial avanza hacia una forma sistémica que participa en acciones y decisiones.

items.title: What type of code should you generate with AI?
items.raw_excerpt:
I (and many people) have been thinking a lot about "what are the best tasks to do using AI."
My personal framework I've been using is, you should use AI to generate code when: 1. The code is easy to validate 2. It is not important that a human understands it I find that the best thing to AI generate is something on the level of a pure function (easy to validate + not necessarily important to understand implementation as long as you understand the interface). I've tried doing things like generating whole services or applications, but those often violate rule 1 - it's hard to validate an entire application behaves "correctly" when "correctly" isn't really well defined - i.e., are there memory leaks, is it secure, is it able to be monitored, etc. I'm curious of others thoughts on this topic.
